learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover the invisible link between electricity and magnetism! Learn how electric currents create magnetic fields to power motors and electromagnets.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A magnetic field is the area around a magnet where its force can be felt. Field lines always emerge from the North pole and merge at the South pole. They never intersect each other.

A wire carrying electric current produces a magnetic field around it. You can find its direction using the 'Right-Hand Thumb Rule' (point thumb in direction of current, wrapped fingers show magnetic field direction).

A coil of many circular turns of wire is a Solenoid. When current flows, it behaves exactly like a bar magnet. Inserting a soft iron core inside it makes a powerful temporary magnet called an Electromagnet.

When a current-carrying wire is placed in a magnetic field, it experiences a physical force. The direction of this force is found using 'Fleming's Left-Hand Rule' (FBI: Force=Thumb, Magnetic Field=Index finger, Current=Middle finger).
Homes receive AC power (220V in India). Circuits have 3 wires: Live (red/brown), Neutral (black/blue), and Earth (green). Earthing prevents severe electric shocks if an appliance leaks current.

fun_activity.title: 🧭 The Compass Wire Test
fun_activity.instructions: Place a small compass on a table. Connect a wire to a battery and hold the wire directly above the compass. The moment you connect the circuit, the compass needle will deflect! This proves electricity creates magnetism (Oersted's discovery).

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly state the rules: Right-Hand Thumb Rule is for finding the magnetic field direction; Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is for finding the Force (motion) direction.
📌 Note: Magnetic field lines inside a solenoid are parallel straight lines, indicating a uniform magnetic field.
📌 Differentiate between a permanent magnet (cannot easily lose magnetism) and an electromagnet (can be turned on/off).
quick_recap: ⭐ Hans Christian Oersted was the first to discover that electricity and magnetism are linked.
⭐ A short circuit happens when the live wire and neutral wire come into direct contact, causing a huge current spike.
⭐ The Earth wire is a safety measure to direct leaking current straight into the ground.
